cultural.vision_reason: Studio portrait of a group of named Kiowa and Cheyenne chiefs and women in traditional dress (fringed shirts, leggings, blankets, jewelry), a documentary photo directly matching the claimed Kiowa ethnicity and dress/daily-life criteria.

physical.title: photographic print (black and white); album
physical.summary:
Photograph (black and white) from an album; studio portrait of a group of Kiowa and Cheyenne people Yellow Bison Bull a Kiowa chief, Yellow Bear a Kiowa chief, Lone Wolf a Kiowa chief,  Little Heart a Kiowa chief, Yellow Wolf a Cheyenne chief, Coy a Kiowa woman and Etla a Kiowa woman; Yellow Bison Bull is seated wearing a decorated fringed shirt, leggings, moccasins, with a wool blanket over one shoulder; Yellow Bear is seated wearing a jacket, a cloth shirt, a neck tie and a woven hat; Lone Wolf is seated wearing a military jacket, and holding a tomahawk; Little Heart is seated wearing a jacket, a neck scarf, shell ear ornaments and a wool blanket over his knees, he is holding a bag; Yellow Wolf is seated wearing a fringed shirt, decorated with quillwork and beadwork, and a peace medal, he has a bison robe over his knees; Coy is seated on the ground wearing a patterned cloth dress, shell ear ornaments, and a blanket around her shoulders; Etla is seated on the ground wearing a fringed dress, leggings and a blanket around her shoulders; Leavenworth, United States of America 
Albumen print
